subject: general
question: In which year Namami Gange Programme is an Integrated Conservation Mission approved as a Flagship Programme by the Union Government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Namami Gange Programme:

 
 
• ​It was started in 2014.
 
• Namami Gange Programme is an Integrated Conservation Mission, approved by the Government of India.
 
• It was started with a budget outlay of Rs.20,000 Crore to accomplish the twin objectives of effective abatement of pollution, conservation, and rejuvenation of National River Ganga.
 
• The River Ganga is important not only for its cultural and spiritual significance but also because it hosts more than 40% of the country’s population.
 
• 8 states are covered under the project including Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• The main pillars of this programme include Biodiversity, Riverfront Development, Sewage Treatment Infrastructure, River Surface Cleaning, Public Awareness, Afforestation, Ganga Gram and Industrial Effluent Monitoring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Namami Gange Programme has been started in order to protect and clean the Ganga. The programme is 100% centrally funded. It intends to ramp up the progress of the Ganga clean-up mission.
 
• **8 states are covered under the project including** Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand. The main pillars of this programme include Biodiversity, Riverfront Development, Sewage Treatment Infrastructure, River Surface Cleaning, Public Awareness, Afforestation, Ganga Gram and Industrial Effluent Monitoring.
